Subjective:
- Current issues:
  - Wheezing and shortness of breath for 2–3 days.
  - Non-productive cough.
  - Reports “fever,” but self-checked temperature 37°C.
  - Exertional dyspnea: unable to walk to work; sometimes struggles to complete sentences during episodes; currently feels well at rest; able to climb stairs.
  - Denies chest pain, hemoptysis, and nocturnal awakenings.
- Past medical history:
  - Asthma in childhood (“quite bad”); required inhalers; occasional hospital visits (no ICU); missed school at times.
  - Hay fever (allergic rhinitis).
  - History of eczema.
  - Adult episodes of similar symptoms in past (timing unclear).
- Medications:
  - Salbutamol (albuterol) inhaler — patient reports using as needed “every few weeks” and around exercise; exact dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Not taking medication for hay fever currently.
- Social history:
  - Non-smoker.
  - Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine every 2–3 days.
  - Lives with partner.
  - Occupation: Engineer; currently working from home/occasional sick leave due to symptoms.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies.

Objective:
- Examination (telemedicine):
  - No in-person exam performed.
  - Patient reports feeling well at rest during consultation; no acute distress reported.
  - Respiratory symptoms as above; no chest pain; no productive cough; no hemoptysis; no nocturnal symptoms.
- Vitals:
  - Self-reported temperature: 37°C.
- Investigations:
  - None performed during visit.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute asthma exacerbation:
   - Assessment: Likely acute asthma exacerbation.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Increase short-acting bronchodilator use: take salbutamol 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially (use with spacer).
     - Prescribe spacer device; pharmacist to demonstrate proper use.
     - Prescribe peak flow meter; patient to record peak flow twice daily (morning and evening) for the next week.
   - Follow-up:
     - Arrange asthma review in approximately 1 week to assess control and review peak flow readings; may need to start additional medication depending on review (specific agent not documented).
     - Safety-netting: Call back urgently if temperature becomes high or wheezing/shortness of breath worsens.
   - Patient education:
     - Pharmacist to teach inhaler/spacer technique.

2. Allergic rhinitis (hay fever):
   - Assessment: Symptomatic hay fever.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Start regular over-the-counter antihistamine (specific agent/dose not documented); clinician to note recommendation in chart.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements:
  - No objective respiratory exam findings (telemedicine).
  - No documentation of salbutamol exact dose/strength or frequency beyond “as needed.”
  - No baseline peak flow or personal best.
  - No documented asthma action plan or controller therapy history beyond childhood.
  - Immunization and recent infection exposure history not discussed.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Patient stated asthma “stopped” ~3–4 years ago (not taking medication), yet later reported “normally” using salbutamol as needed — conflict noted.
  - Patient reported having “fever,” but measured temperature was 37°C (normal) — conflict noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Some pauses and clarifications; a few unclear responses, but key clinical details largely obtainable.
